svg.text: Reported top-1 reduction, in the order the paper presents the ingredients — not a ranking
Bar length is the top-1 error reduction, in percentage points, reported for that ingredient alone. Hatched rows: called necessary, never measured.

g.data-tip: Not on this axis at all. Its evidence is Figure 1: six times fewer epochs to reach 25% training error on CIFAR-10 with a four-layer net. A speed claim, not an accuracy claim.
g.text: 6× fewer epochs to 25% train error — speed, not accuracy

g.data-tip: Compared against a one-GPU net with half as many kernels per convolutional layer, except its last conv and fc layers, which footnote 2 says were left full size. Read the 1.7% as the gain of a bigger net, not of the split topology (slide 10).
g.text: vs one GPU, half the kernels; fn. 2: baseline not fully halved

g.data-tip: Reported as 1.4% top-1 and 1.2% top-5. Its four hyper-parameters were selected on a validation set, and the gain comes with no seeds or error bars.
g.text: vs the same net without it; k, n, α, β tuned on validation

g.data-tip: 0.4% top-1 and 0.3% top-5 against s = 2, z = 2, which produces output of equivalent dimensions. That equality is what makes it the cleanest comparison in the paper.
g.text: vs s = 2, z = 2 at identical output size — the cleanest one

g.data-tip: Also unmeasured. The paper says only that without this scheme the network suffers substantial overfitting, which would have forced much smaller networks.
g.text: no number — without it, substantial overfitting

g.data-tip: The paper says this scheme reduces the top-1 error rate by over 1%. It is the only augmentation number in the paper, and the bound is one-sided.
g.text: vs no colour jitter — a lower bound, not a measurement

g.data-tip: No error number is reported. The paper says only that without dropout the network exhibits substantial overfitting, and that dropout roughly doubles the iterations to converge.
g.text: no number — without it, substantial overfitting

g.data-tip: §7 reports that removing any of the middle layers costs about 2% of top-1 performance. One deletion, one number, no seeds and no reported re-tuning.
g.text: removing any one middle layer, Sec 7 — a single probe

svg.text: Why the bar lengths cannot be compared
Each bar has its own baseline, dataset and scope, and no experiment varies two ingredients together — so the bars cannot be added or ordered.
And the two ingredients the authors call necessary — dropout and the crops — are exactly the two with no bar at all.
